We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-aniline.

We need 3 reactions: likely (1) sulfonamide formation (attach sulfonyl chloride to aniline). (2) amide formation via coupling of carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) with aniline. (3) Doebner modification to create the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (N-phenyl). Gives precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (C= C-COOH attached to phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then disconnect sulfonamide: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline (the p-tolyl amine). Actually the sulfonamide is attached to the p-tolyl amine (the first phenyl with methyl). So we have p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl sulfonyl group (the phenyl bearing the unsaturated chain). So precursor: p-toluidine (C c1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride: c1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1 attached to the other phenyl (the same phenyl as unsaturated chain). Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl that also bears the unsaturated chain. So we need a phenyl sulfonyl chloride with the unsaturated chain attached at para position? In target, the sulfonyl phenyl is attached to the unsaturated chain at para? Let's examine: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) has the unsaturated amide substituent at para relative to the sulfonamide attachment? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The sulfonamide attaches at position 1 of that phenyl (the S attached to N). The unsaturated chain is at position 4 (para). So the phenyl ring has two substituents: sulfonyl attached to N (via S) and the α,β-unsaturated amide chain.

Thus retrosynthesis step 2: disconnect the C-C bond forming the α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde via Doebner modification. So we need aromatic aldehyde (para-substituted phenyl with sulfonyl group?) Actually the aldehyde would be the phenyl with sulfonyl group at position 1 and aldehyde at para (position 4). So precursor: p-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2 with sulfonyl group attached). Then Doebner with malonic acid gives the α,β-unsaturated acid.

Thus overall three steps:

Step A (forward): coupling of carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) with aniline to give amide (amide formation). Retrosynthetic: break amide bond to give acid and aniline.

Step B: sulfonamide formation: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and p-toluidine. Since we have p-tolyl sulfonamide attached to the phenyl sulfonyl group. So we need p-toluidine (4-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride derived from the phenyl-sulfonyl (the same phenyl that also has the unsaturated chain). So we need to generate sulfonyl chloride from that phenyl (maybe via chlorosulfonation). But for retrosynthesis we can just propose sulfonyl chloride.

Step C: Doebner modification: break the C=C bond and decarboxylation to give aldehyde and malonic acid. So we need aromatic aldehyde (para-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The unsaturated acid is formed from aldehyde + malonic acid.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with type "mol" root target, children: reaction nodes each with template_id (we need actual IDs). We need to search for templates matching each transformation.

Let's search for amide formation template: functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, functional_groups_formed: amide. Use search.
